summary: Working in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, Samani Pratibha Pragya completed her PhD at SOAS University of London between 2011 and 2017. She is attested as a research assistant at SOAS in 2020.

Specializing in Indology, Sambhavi Ganesh studied at Lady Shri Ram College, the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, and the University of Edinburgh (PhD, 2020–2024) under Radhika Govinda. Her posts include Kudumbashree (2019–2020) and King's College London (2025–2026).

Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He served at the University of Calcutta from circa 1978 to 2005 and is attested as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Sampadananda Mishra studied at Pondicherry University (ca. 1996–2001). He later served as Director at Rishihood University in 2021 and as Professor at Hindu University of America in 2022.
Active in Indology, Sampan Chakrabarty completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Pallab Sengupta. He is attested as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Drepung Monastery, SOAS, and the University of London under David Snellgrove, he held posts at CNRS, SOAS, and served as President of the IATS (1995–2000).

Samuel Beal was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Trinity College, Cambridge, and Durham University, he held posts at Bramham College, the India Office Records, and was Professor of Chinese at University College London (1877).

Samuel Charles Hill worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at University College London, he served in the Bengal Educational Service (1881–1912), taught at Dhaka College (1881), and headed records at the National Archives of India and BNF (1899–1912).
Samuel Charters Macpherson was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his education at the University of Edinburgh (1822–1823) and Trinity College, Cambridge.

Samuel De Coster Atkins was an Indologist and linguist who earned his A.B. and Ph.D. at Princeton University. After working as an assistant at Baylor University (1935–1937), he taught Classics and Sanskrit at Princeton from 1937 to 1978.

Samuel George Frederick Brandon was a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leeds (ca. 1927–1930) and held an academic post at the University of Manchester from circa 1951 to 1971.

Samuel Gottlieb Rudolf Henzi studied at Bern, Tübingen, and Göttingen, and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Chézy. In 1820, he was appointed Professor of Exegesis and Oriental Languages at the University of Tartu.

Samuel Grant Oliphant was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Princeton and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He taught at several institutions, including Parsons College, Olivet, and Grove City College, where he was Professor of Greek in 1911.
Samuel Heinrich Ribbach was active in the field of Tibetology. He served as a missionary for the Moravian Church between 1892 and 1927 and later held a post at the Museum am Rothenbaum.

Samuel Henry Butcher was educated at Marlborough College and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held academic appointments at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1882 to 1903 and at Harvard University around 1904.

Samuel Henry Kellogg was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Educated at Princeton University and Princeton Theological Seminary, he served as an instructor at Allahabad Theological Training School (1873–1876) and Professor of Systematic Theology at Pittsburgh Theological Seminary (1877–1885).

Samuel Johnson was a scholar in the fields of linguistics and other disciplines. He completed his education at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College in Stourbridge, and Pembroke College, Oxford (1728–1731).

Samuel M. Grupper worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, where he studied under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.

Samuel Mateer was active in Indology and religious studies. After studying at Bedford Theological College from circa 1856 to 1858, he served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society from 1859 to 1891.

Samuel Ross Winans was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Princeton University (A.B. ca. 1870–1874). He served at Princeton as Professor of Greek and Instructor of Sanskrit (1876–1883) and later as dean of the faculty (1899–1903).
